newsitem.title: USA: U.S. refiners shun foreign crudes, Latam quiet.
newsitem.headline: U.S. refiners shun foreign crudes, Latam quiet.

text.p: U.S. refiners continued to shun foreign crudes Monday, reflecting the closed arbitrage between benchmarks West Texas Intermediate and North Sea Brent, trade sources said.
The spread between WTI and Brent stood around $1.20-25 a barrel, up five cents from late Friday.
"Arb opportunities, even on dated Brent, are likely to stay closed through February," said Ken Miller, senior principal at Houston-based Purvin & Gertz.
A Wall Street trader was heard offering a delivered Brent cargo at January WTI plus 50 cents.
"At those prices, most refiners are going to lie low," said one trader.
The closed window has lifted prices for alternative domestic grades such as Light Louisiana Sweet, which was trading Monday at around WTI/Cushing plus 88-90 cents.

The Latin American spot scene was quiet relative to recent weeks, although state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela S.A. (PdVSA) was reported to have picked up anywhere from two to five cargoes of Ecuadoran Oriente crude for its Curacao refinery.
In the U.S. paper market, a Wall Street trader bought a series of Brent partials $24.10 a barrel, two cents higher than the IPE settlement price.
The Jan/Feb Brent spread changed hands twice among Wall Street players at 61 cents, off one cent from the London close.
